title: The Influence of Ovarian Hormones on Patella and Achilles Tendon Stiffness Across the Menstrual Cycle: A Prospective Cohort Study
summary:
During the menstrual cycle, the levels of female sex hormones change naturally. These hormonal changes may also influence the properties of tendons, but scientific evidence is still limited.
The aim of this study is to investigate whether the stiffness of the patellar tendon and the Achilles tendon changes during the menstrual cycle and whether these changes are related to the natural fluctuations in hormone levels.
Healthy women will be examined at three time points during one menstrual cycle. At each visit, a small blood sample will be collected to measure hormone levels, and the tendons will be examined using two non-invasive measurement techniques. The findings will improve our understanding of how the menstrual cycle may affect tendon properties.

interventions.name: The planned investigation is a prospective cohort study in which participants are assessed throughout one menstrual cycle. The aim is to investigate changes in the stiffness of the patellar and Achilles tendons in relation to the physiological fluctuations of sex hormones during the menstrual cycle.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- women of reproductive age
-regular ovulatory menstrual cycle with a cycle length between 21 and 35 days
-physically active, performing at least 2 hours of moderate-intensity physical activity per week
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute injuries, disorders, or inflammation of the patellar or Achilles tendon, or of the knee or ankle joint in at least one lower extremity
- Gynecological disorders (e.g., polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) or endometriosis)
- Use of hormonal contraception (e.g., oral contraceptives, intrauterine devices/systems, contraceptive implants, vaginal ring, or injectable contraceptives)
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Menstrual cycle irregularities (e.g., amenorrhea, oligomenorrhea, or polymenorrhea)
